subject: Temporary retention carveout & backup purge sequencing — DPA impact
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha@medwell.io>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops@medwell.io, legal@medwell.io
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Coordination: temporary retain window + backup purge sequencing

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an upcoming audit and need to lock down how Redwood will handle a short-term retain for a scoped set of records while the auditor completes their work. Two specific asks:

1) Can Redwood pause the scheduled backup purge for a specific customer snapshot (MedWell-Prod-2026-09) for up to 21 days without impacting the global purge SLA?
2) For logs associated with the snapshot, can you provide an exception path so we keep a copy for forensic review but still honor our DPA obligations for deletion timelines once the hold is released?

Attached are our proposed DPA redlines (MedWell_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a rough timeline spreadsheet (backup-prune-sequence-2026-10.xlsx). Our legal team is CC'd.

High level timeline we’re targeting:
- Audit notice: 2026-10-05
- Snapshot hold start: 2026-10-06 00:00 UTC
- Release window: by 2026-10-27 23:59 UTC (21 days)

Can your team confirm if this is operationally feasible, and whether you need contract language amendments?

Appreciate a quick ack and a proposal for next steps.

— Samantha
MedWell Health, Senior Compliance Analyst

---
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha@medwell.io>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: temporary retain window + backup purge sequencing

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Quick ack: we can run a scoped temporary retain for a single snapshot for up to 21 days, but there are three constraints we should align on before giving final confirmation:

- Technical isolation: we need the snapshot identifier and the list of bucket/volume IDs to ensure the purge job excludes only that data. Markus will outline the ops steps below.
- Forensic logs: Redwood can create a short-term immutable export of the relevant logs to an isolated hold store; however, export retention vs. DPA deletion obligations must be explicit in contract language (Kim will propose wording).
- Cost/operational change: short-term holds require a small storage and retention surcharge and a manual release process if the hold is extended.

Next steps I propose:
1) Markus to send a one-pager (ops steps + rollback) and confirm the exclusion approach.
2) Kim to propose DPA wording for the exception and a short amendment template.
3) I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync with your legal/ops to finalize cadence and DocuSign.

We can meet tomorrow (2026-10-03) or on Monday; what works for your team?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, Samantha Cole <samantha@medwell.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: temporary retain window + backup purge sequencing

Hi all —

Operational note (summary of the one-pager):

Planned approach to implement scoped temporary retain for snapshot MedWell-Prod-2026-09:

1) Identification — Ops needs the snapshot UUID(s) and a full list of associated log prefixes (e.g., /prod/medwell/2026/09/). Once provided we will create an exclusion filter for the scheduled prune job.

2) Immutability export — For forensic review we will generate a read-only immutable export of the matching logs to a dedicated hold bucket with object-lock enabled for the hold duration. Export will be tagged with hold-id: MW-HOLD-20261006.

3) Isolation & monitoring — The exclusion will be scoped to the single customer snapshot; global purge pipeline will continue to run normally for all other snapshots. We’ll add a per-run alert and retention-metering so support can easily verify the hold.

4) Release / Automatic cleanup — On release we will (a) remove the exclusion so subsequent purge runs can clean up, and (b) delete the immutable export after a configurable grace period (default 48 hours) once legal confirms release.

Operational constraints / caveats:
- We cannot hold incremental rolling snapshots for >21 days on the same hold-id without additional resource reservations.
- If the hold is extended beyond 21 days we require a manual capacity reservation and a PO or surcharge agreement.
- Legal/contract clarity required for exported logs: whether the immutable export is considered a retained copy under the DPA (Kim, see below).

I can prepare the exact ops playbook and run commands; please confirm the snapshot UUIDs and whether MedWell wants the immutable export to remain in Redwood-managed storage or pushed to a MedWell-controlled S3 bucket.

— Markus
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference

---
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, Samantha Cole <samantha@medwell.io>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: temporary retain window + backup purge sequencing

Hi Samantha —

I reviewed your redlines and sketched a narrow amendment that covers a temporary forensic hold without creating a permanent carveout from deletion obligations. Key points of the proposed amendment (high level):

- Temporary Forensic Hold: Customer may request a scoped temporary hold for a specific snapshot ID for a maximum of 21 calendar days. Redwood will implement operational holds as described in the ops playbook.

- Export Treatment: Any immutable export created by Redwood for forensic review shall be considered a transient operational copy and will be deleted within 48 hours of hold release unless the Customer explicitly requests the export be delivered to a Customer-controlled location (delivery requires written confirmation and may trigger export fees).

- Auditability & Logging: Redwood will maintain an immutable event record (retention metadata, hold-id, timestamps) for a period of 12 months for evidentiary purposes. This record consists of metadata only and not the retained payload.

- Fees & Extensions: Holds beyond 21 days require a separate agreement.

Suggested next steps:
- I’ll produce a short amendment (tracked changes) for your legal team to review.
- Ben: once MedWell confirms ops choices (Redwood-managed export vs. customer push) we’ll include the final language and route to DocuSign.

I attached the redline I referenced (MedWell_DPA_redline_v3.docx) with inline comments.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel — Redwood Inference

- Export destination: we prefer Redwood to create the immutable export in Redwood-managed storage and then provide a verified transfer (SHA256 manifest) to our ops team. If we later request delivery to our S3, we’ll provide written confirmation.

Please send the DPA amendment for review and the DocuSign link once ready. Also, Markus — can you confirm the expected time window for the first excluded prune run after we flip the hold? We want to ensure the snapshot is excluded before any scheduled run on 2026-10-06 00:00 UTC.

— Samantha
